config.title: Unnecessary Re-renders

intro.title: Unnecessary Re-renders
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays a list of items and a counter. You will learn how to identify and prevent unnecessary re-renders, which occur when parts of your component update without any actual data changes. The core concept involves using Vue's reactivity system and the `v-for` directive efficiently. You will work with Vue's template syntax, reactive data properties, and the `key` attribute to optimize rendering. By the end, you'll understand how to make your Vue apps faster by avoiding wasteful updates.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications like interactive dashboards with live charts and data tables, unnecessary re-renders can severely degrade performance. For example, when a user filters a large dataset, only the table component should update, not the entire dashboard including static headers and sidebars. Similarly, in complex forms with multiple input sections, changing one field should not cause re-renders of unrelated validation messages or submit buttons. Mastering re-render control is essential for building smooth, responsive user interfaces in data-intensive Vue applications.

objectives: Identify components that trigger unnecessary re-renders in Vue applications
Apply computed properties to optimize reactive data transformations
Implement watchers to control side effects and prevent redundant updates
Configure component lifecycle hooks to manage rendering behavior
Manipulate reactive data structures to minimize cascading re-renders
Bind event handlers efficiently to avoid performance bottlenecks
Construct memoized functions to cache expensive calculations

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue framework functionality.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the import statement needs both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package. Check that you're importing both symbols correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is incorrect. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package using the import syntax.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'UnnecessaryRendersDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a component using Vue's defineComponent or a simple function that returns an object from setup.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create a Vue component named 'UnnecessaryRendersDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a basic Vue component structure ready for adding state and UI.
successCriteria: The component 'UnnecessaryRendersDemo' is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named 'UnnecessaryRendersDemo' with a setup function that returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Create a Vue component named 'UnnecessaryRendersDemo' with a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your UnnecessaryRendersDemo component, declare two reactive state variables using ref: one named 'count' initialized to 0, and another named 'unrelatedValue' initialized to 100.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported earlier to create reactive references. Remember to declare them inside the setup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has two reactive state variables: count starting at 0 and unrelatedValue starting at 100.
successCriteria: Two ref variables are declared inside the setup function: count initialized to 0 and unrelatedValue initialized to 100.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created at least one reactive variable, but make sure you have both count and unrelatedValue declared with ref inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the ref function to create both variables inside the setup function, with the correct initial values.

steps.title: Define increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named increment that increases the count value by 1.
steps.hint: Create a regular JavaScript function that updates the reactive count value using .value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The increment function is defined and will update the count state when called.
successCriteria: The increment function is defined inside setup and updates count.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the function is named 'increment' and it updates count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that increases count.value by 1.

steps.title: Return state and handlers from setup
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, return an object containing count, unrelatedValue, increment, and updateUnrelated so they become available in the template.
steps.hint: The return statement should be the last line inside setup(). Return an object with the reactive state variables and handler functions you've created.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object with all reactive state and handler functions, making them accessible to the template.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object containing count, unrelatedValue, increment, and updateUnrelated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning all four items: count, unrelatedValue, increment, and updateUnrelated. Check that you haven't missed any.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function needs to return an object with all the reactive state variables and handler functions. Look at the code you've written so far and return those values.

steps.title: Add template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section with a container div in your component.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can add a template section by including a template property in your component object. Inside it, return a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic template structure with a container div.
successCriteria: The component includes a template property with a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the template property with a div element inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing. Add a template property with a div element to your component.

steps.title: Display count value and add increment button
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current count value and a button element with @click bound to the increment handler.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive state values in the template. The button should trigger the increment function when clicked.
steps.analogousExample: Current value: {{ value }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the count value and an increment button that can trigger state updates.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element displaying count value and a button with @click bound to increment handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the paragraph showing count value and the button with @click bound to increment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the count value and increment button. Add a paragraph with {{ count }} and a button with @click="increment".

steps.title: Display unrelated value and add update button
steps.instruction: In the template, add a paragraph that displays the unrelatedValue and a button with @click bound to the updateUnrelated handler.
steps.hint: Use the same pattern as the count display: a paragraph with text and interpolation, and a button with @click.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI now shows both the count and unrelated value with their respective update buttons.
successCriteria: A paragraph displays unrelatedValue and a button with @click="updateUnrelated" is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure you have both the paragraph showing unrelatedValue and the button wired to updateUnrelated.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should include a paragraph with {{ unrelatedValue }} and a button with @click="updateUnrelated".

steps.title: Add console log to demonstrate re-renders
steps.instruction: Add a console.log statement inside the template to log a message each time the component renders.
steps.hint: Place the console.log directly in the template section, not inside setup().
steps.analogousExample:
// Logging in template template: `

Count: {{ count }}

Unrelated: {{ unrelatedValue }}

{{ console.log('Component rendered') }}
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will log 'Component rendered' to the console each time it re-renders, demonstrating unnecessary re-renders when unrelated state changes.
successCriteria: A console.log statement is added inside the template to log a message on every render.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the console.log is placed directly in the template section (not inside setup()) so it executes on every render.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a console.log statement inside the template to log a message like 'Component rendered'. This will help demonstrate when the component re-renders.
